land.text: the Sierra Leone Colony and Protectorate: 'the formal recognition of the territory as the Sierra Leone Colony and Protectorate'

predecessors.note: Cliopatria's British Africa shape of 1960 holds Sierra Leone (344 of the country's 351 grid cells); its British East Africa row of 1961 no longer does.

keyframe_review.note: 74,220 km2 for 1961-2023 against the infobox's 73,252 km2 (no year; land 73,132 plus water 120), ratio 1.01. The page records no border change or dispute (it says only 'bordered by Guinea to the north and east, Liberia to the southeast'). The civil war of 1991-2002 moved no frontier; the land the RUF held is in the ledger as loss/gain against revolutionary-united-front.

region.text: Sierra Leone, formerly the Sierra Leone Colony and Protectorate

ledger.note: 1961-04-27: Sierra Leone becomes independent. 'On 27 April 1961, Margai led Sierra Leone to independence from Great Britain' (infobox: 'Dominion: 27 April 1961').
1971-04-19: Sierra Leone becomes a republic. 'On 19 April 1971, when Sierra Leone became a republic', Stevens became president under a new constitution. No change of territory.

region.text: 'large swathes of territory in eastern and southern Sierra Leone'

ledger.note: 1991-03-23: the civil war begins. The conflict 'began on 23 March 1991 when the Revolutionary United Front (RUF)' launched its intervention, backed by Charles Taylor's NPFL (the RUF page: it 'led elements of the National Patriotic Front of Liberia across the Liberian border'). The zone is the east and south that the page names; the fighting reached Freetown's outskirts in 1995 and the capital in 1997 and 1999, which the zone does not show.

region.text: 'large swathes of territory in eastern and southern Sierra Leone'

ledger.note: 1991 (from the invasion of 23 March, over the first year): the RUF holds the east and south. 'During the first year of the war, the RUF took control of large swathes of territory in eastern and southern Sierra Leone.' The page names provinces, not districts, so the region is the two provinces as a ceiling.

minus.text: the strip along the Sierra Leone-Liberian border to which the SLA 'pushed the RUF' in March 1993

region.text: the eastern and southern swathes except the Liberian border strip: the SLA 'recaptured the Koidu and Kono diamond districts and pushed the RUF to the Sierra Leone - Liberia border' in March 1993

ledger.note: 1993-03: the army recaptures the diamond districts. 'the SLA recaptured the Koidu and Kono diamond districts and pushed the RUF to the Sierra Leone - Liberia border.' The width of the border strip the RUF kept is not given (drawn three cells wide).

region.text: 'much of the diamond-rich Eastern Province' held by the RUF by 1994

ledger.note: 1994: the RUF again holds the Eastern Province. 'by 1994 they had gained control of much of the diamond-rich Eastern Province' (Sierra Leone page). The civil war page adds that in January 1995 RUF forces seized the SIEROMCO bauxite and Sierra Rutile mines in the southwest and in March 1995 were 'within twenty miles of Freetown'; it does not say how long they held them.

union.text: the strip along the Sierra Leone-Liberian border to which the SLA 'pushed the RUF' in March 1993

region.text: the rebel-held areas: the Eastern Province and the border strip, where 'UN forces moved into rebel-held areas and began to disarm rebel soldiers' in 2001 and the war was declared over on 18 January 2002

ledger.note: 2002-01-18: the war is declared over and the rebel-held areas return to the state. 'On 18 January 2002, President Kabbah declared the Sierra Leone Civil War over'; 'In 2001, UN forces moved into rebel-held areas and began to disarm rebel soldiers' (Sierra Leone page). The pages do not map the rebel-held ground between 1995 and 2001 (they record the May 1997 AFRC coup, Freetown retaken by ECOMOG in March 1998 and the attack of January 1999), so this region bridges a silence.

region.text: 'large swathes of territory in eastern and southern Sierra Leone'

ledger.note: 2002-01-18: 'President Kabbah declared the Sierra Leone Civil War over' (infobox: 23 March 1991 - 18 January 2002, 'Commonwealth victory'); the RUF became a political party after the peace.

wars.name: Sierra Leone Civil War
belligerents: Liberia (Charles Taylor's National Patriotic Front of Liberia)

zones.text: 'large swathes of territory in eastern and southern Sierra Leone'
the strip along the Sierra Leone-Liberian border to which the SLA 'pushed the RUF' in March 1993

wars.outcome: Government victory, helped by Executive Outcomes (1995-96), ECOMOG (1998-2000), British paratroopers (Operation Palliser, 2000) and the UN mission; about 50,000 killed; Kabbah declared the war over on 18 January 2002. No change of frontier.
wars.note: The page dates the Lomé accord both 7 July 1999 and 27 March 1999 and gives March 1998, not February, for ECOMOG's recapture of Freetown (the Sierra Leone page says February 1998 for Kabbah's reinstatement). The zones are the provinces the pages name, not mapped front lines.

certainty.note: Inherited colonial frontiers with Guinea and Liberia; the page records no dispute (it does not mention Yenga). The rebel-held areas of 1991-2002 were never mapped on the pages opened and are soft.

sources.title: Sierra Leone
sources.note: Infobox area (73,252 km2), Freetown, independence 27 April 1961, republic 19 April 1971, RUF in the Eastern Province by 1994, UN forces in rebel-held areas 2001.

sources.title: Sierra Leone Civil War
sources.note: 23 March 1991 - 18 January 2002; RUF swathes in 1991; Koidu and Kono recaptured March 1993; the AFRC coup of May 1997; ECOMOG March 1998; January 1999; Operation Palliser.

sources.title: Revolutionary United Front
sources.note: Used for the rebel dossier: thin on territory (infobox 'Liberated Zone (1991-2002)'), transformation into a party after the peace.

notes: Sierra Leone: Cliopatria row 'Sierra Leone' 1961..2024 (two identical shapes), reviewed with three pages (the third, the RUF article, for the rebel dossier). (1) The state's frontiers did not move; the civil war is recorded as a contest over the east and south plus loss/gain events against a new rebel dossier, revolutionary-united-front (written in this batch, thin: the pages give only 1991 'large swathes' of the east and south, the recapture of Kono in March 1993, 'much of the diamond-rich Eastern Province' by 1994, and 'rebel-held areas' in 2001; nothing maps the years 1995-2000). A gap-filler should open the Sierra Leone Civil War article's section on the RUF's 'Liberated Zone', Kailahun and Kono district control and the 1997-98 AFRC junta, which is not drawn here. (2) The Freetown episodes (1995 'within twenty miles', May 1997 AFRC/RUF capture, March 1998 ECOMOG recapture, January 1999) are in notes, not zones. (3) The Sierra Leone page gives no president list; identity.rulers omitted. (4) The border_band regions refer to the Cliopatria shapes of sierra-leone and republic-of-liberia in 1993. (5) No gazetteer names were needed.
